---
title: "Sea ice retreat and the ice-edge bloom"
subtitle: "Southern Ocean, 1997-2025"
---

When sea ice retreats in spring and summer it leaves behind a surface layer
that is often freshened, stratified and well lit, and chlorophyll rises in
the weeks that follow: the ice-edge bloom. This site follows that bloom
around Antarctica for 29 seasons, by lining up satellite ocean colour with
the day each place lost its sea ice, and asks what sets its size and timing.

It is part of the trend.* family of open, self-updating Southern Ocean
records (sea surface temperature, sea level, chlorophyll, and now sea ice).

## What we find

- **The bloom follows retreat.** Over the whole record, median chlorophyll
  rises from about 0.2 mg m^-3^ a month before retreat to about 0.34 mg m^-3^
  a month after it (1.5x the pre-retreat mean), then decays back to the
  pre-retreat level by about four months after retreat.
- **Retreat timing orders the bloom.** Early (spring) retreats give slow,
  broad, late-peaking blooms; mid-season retreats the sharpest and largest;
  late retreats start from an already high level and peak within about two
  weeks. Against open water at the same latitude, sector and date, the
  later the retreat the larger and faster the rise (about 1.2x, 1.4x and
  1.8x the open-water level for early, mid and late retreat).
- **The continental shelf carries the strongest blooms.** About 5% of the
  data, but blooms there reach about 5x the open-water level and stay high
  for two months; late-retreat shelf water (polynyas, coastal leads) is
  already productive before the ice formally retreats.
- **Ice-edge contamination is not the explanation.** Removing pixels with
  ice nearby *raises* the pre-retreat level rather than lowering it.
- **Physics matters most for spring retreats.** In a reanalysis of the
  ocean state after retreat, deeper mixing and saltier surface water lower
  the bloom peak for early retreats (strongest in the Ross and
  Bellingshausen-Amundsen sectors); for summer retreats, already shallow and
  well lit, the physical state explains little.
- **Year to year, the effect of retreat timing changes sign with place.**
  In the outer pack (spring retreat) a later than usual retreat gives a
  bigger bloom; further south (summer retreat) a later retreat gives a
  smaller one. Pooled, these cancel. Mixing, temperature and salinity
  explain little of the year-to-year variation; the likely missing driver
  is iron supply.
